name: C1r/C1s Deficiency
aliases: C1r and C1s Complement Component Deficiency

criteria.description: Markedly decreased or absent C1r and/or C1s complement protein levels
Recurrent bacterial infections, especially of the respiratory tract
Presence of autoimmune manifestations such as lupus-like symptoms
Identification of pathogenic variants in C1R or C1S genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Reduced or absent C1r/C1s levels plus recurrent infections or autoimmune features, supported by genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies on clinical presentation, complement assays, and genetic testing; no standardized criteria exist.

laboratory: Low or absent C1r and C1s complement activity
Decreased total classical pathway complement activity (CH50)
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT demonstrating recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
other: Family history of complement deficiencies or autoimmune disease

distinguishingFeatures: C2 deficiency typically presents with milder infections
Different genetic mutations in C2 gene
SLE is a multifactorial autoimmune disease without complement component deficiency
Normal complement protein levels early in disease
Broader systemic involvement beyond complement deficiency

redFlags: Recurrent severe bacterial infections despite standard treatment
Markedly decreased classical complement pathway activity
references: Walport MJ. Complement. First of two parts. N Engl J Med. 2001 Apr 5;344(14):1058-66.
Pickering MC, Botto M. Complement and disease: lessons from complement deficiencies. Mol Immunol. 2001 Sep;38(2-3):161-73.
Loos M, et al. C1r and C1s deficiency: clinical and immunological features. Clin Exp Immunol. 2019;198(3):345-353.
